modulesynopsis.name: mod_proxy_nng
modulesynopsis.description: Dynamic Balancer membership where backends announce themselves to the reverse proxy over an nng PUB/SUB channel

summary.p: This module lets backend servers announce themselves to a front-end reverse proxy, which then adds each announcing backend as a live member (worker) of a mod_proxy_balancer balancer. When a backend stops announcing, the proxy takes it out of rotation. This provides self-registering, self-healing balancer membership without editing the proxy configuration or driving the balancer-manager by hand.

Communication uses the PUB/SUB pattern of the nng (nanomsg-next-generation) library. Because an nng PUB socket is send-only, the direction of the data (backend to proxy) makes each backend the publisher and the reverse proxy the subscriber:

ul.li: The reverse proxy opens a SUB socket and listens on a stable address (ProxyNngSubscribe).
Each backend opens a PUB socket and dials the proxy on startup (ProxyNngPublish), then periodically publishes a short announcement advertising its own routable URL (ProxyNngAdvertise).

summary.p: On the proxy, ProxyNngBalancer names the balancer that announced backends are added to. Membership changes are applied using the same internal mechanism as the balancer-manager web interface, so a backend added this way behaves exactly like a statically configured or manually added BalancerMember, and is visible and editable in the balancer-manager.

This module requires the service of mod_watchdog and mod_proxy_balancer. The background work (listening, publishing, adding and evicting members) runs in a single mod_watchdog child process, so it is not available under the prefork MPM behaviour where that singleton cannot run.

note.title: Authentication
note.p: Any host that can reach the proxy's SUB port could otherwise announce an arbitrary backend URL and cause the proxy to send client traffic to it. Set ProxyNngSecret to the same value on the proxy and on every backend so that announcements are authenticated with a keyed message-authentication code (MAC) and a timestamp. When a secret is configured the proxy drops any announcement that is not validly signed and recent. If no secret is configured the channel is unauthenticated and the proxy logs a warning at startup.

note.title: Confidentiality
note.p: Announcements are authenticated but not encrypted; the payload is operational metadata (backend URLs), not secret data. If transport confidentiality is required, use an nng build with TLS support and a tls+tcp:// URL for ProxyNngSubscribe/ProxyNngPublish.

section.title: Usage example
section.p: The following pair of configurations sets up a self-registering balancer. The backends require no knowledge of each other and the proxy needs no pre-declared BalancerMember entries — only an empty balancer with room to grow.
section.highlight:
# Listen for backend announcements on the cluster network interface. ProxyNngSubscribe tls+tcp://0.0.0.0:5555 ProxyNngSecret "a-long-random-shared-cluster-secret" ProxyNngBalancer cluster
# A backend is dropped from rotation if it does not announce for 30 seconds. ProxyNngTimeout 30
# An initially-empty balancer with spare slots for the dynamic members. <Proxy balancer://cluster> ProxySet growth=16 </Proxy> ProxyPass "/" "balancer://cluster/" ProxyPassReverse "/" "balancer://cluster/"

# Dial the proxy and announce this backend's routable origin every 10 seconds. ProxyNngPublish tls+tcp://proxy.example.com:5555 ProxyNngAdvertise http://10.0.0.5:8080 ProxyNngSecret "a-long-random-shared-cluster-secret" ProxyNngInterval 10
section.p: When a backend starts it dials the proxy and begins publishing. The proxy verifies each announcement against the shared secret, adds http://10.0.0.5:8080 as a member of balancer://cluster, and enables it. If that backend later stops publishing for longer than ProxyNngTimeout, the proxy disables the member (taking it out of rotation); a subsequent announcement re-enables it.

note.p: A backend added at runtime occupies one of the balancer's growth slots for the lifetime of the server process; it is disabled rather than removed when it stops announcing, matching the behaviour of the balancer-manager (which can add, but not remove, workers at runtime). Size growth for the maximum number of backends you expect to register.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngSubscribe
directivesynopsis.description: Address on which the reverse proxy listens for backend announcements

usage.p: The ProxyNngSubscribe directive marks a server as the announcement subscriber (the reverse proxy). It opens an nng SUB socket and listens on the given nng url, e.g. tcp://0.0.0.0:5555 for a plain TCP rendezvous, or tls+tcp://0.0.0.0:5555 when the nng library was built with TLS support.

Backends connect to this address via ProxyNngPublish. The directive should be used together with ProxyNngBalancer; without it, announcements are received and logged but no members are added. ProxyNngSubscribe and ProxyNngPublish are mutually exclusive on the same server.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngPublish
directivesynopsis.description: Address of the reverse proxy that a backend dials to announce itself

usage.p: The ProxyNngPublish directive marks a server as an announcement publisher (a backend). It opens an nng PUB socket and dials the proxy's ProxyNngSubscribe address given by url, e.g. tcp://proxy.example.com:5555. The connection is established in the background and retried automatically, so a backend may be started before the proxy is available.
Use ProxyNngAdvertise to specify the routable URL the backend announces. ProxyNngPublish and ProxyNngSubscribe are mutually exclusive on the same server.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngAdvertise
directivesynopsis.description: The routable URL a backend announces to the reverse proxy

usage.p: The ProxyNngAdvertise directive sets the backend's own reachable origin (for example http://10.0.0.5:8080) that the proxy will add as a BalancerMember. It must be a full scheme://host[:port] URL that the proxy can reach — not the local listen address — and is validated when the configuration is parsed.

This directive is used on a backend, alongside ProxyNngPublish. If it is omitted, the backend still publishes a heartbeat but advertises no URL, so the proxy logs the announcement without adding a member.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngBalancer
directivesynopsis.description: Name of the balancer that announced backends are added to

usage.p: The ProxyNngBalancer directive names the balancer, on the reverse proxy, into which announced backends are inserted as members. Give the bare balancer name (for example cluster for balancer://cluster); a leading balancer:// is accepted and stripped.

The named balancer must exist and have spare capacity. Declare it with a <Proxy> block and a growth setting (or rely on BalancerGrowth) so there are free slots for the dynamically added members. This directive is used together with ProxyNngSubscribe.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngInterval
directivesynopsis.description: How often a backend publishes its announcement

usage.p: The ProxyNngInterval directive sets how frequently a backend (a ProxyNngPublish server) publishes its announcement. It uses the time-interval directive syntax and defaults to seconds; the default is 5 seconds.
The interval must be meaningfully smaller than the proxy's ProxyNngTimeout, so that the occasional lost or delayed announcement does not cause a healthy backend to be evicted.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngTimeout
directivesynopsis.description: How long the proxy waits, without an announcement, before a backend is taken out of rotation

usage.p: The ProxyNngTimeout directive sets how long the reverse proxy will wait for an announcement from a backend before disabling that backend's balancer member (taking it out of rotation). A later announcement from the same backend re-enables it. It uses the time-interval directive syntax and defaults to seconds.

The default, 0, disables eviction entirely: backends are added when they announce but are never automatically removed. Set this to a small multiple of the backends' ProxyNngInterval to enable self-healing membership. This directive is used on the proxy.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngSecret
directivesynopsis.description: Pre-shared secret used to authenticate announcements

usage.p: The ProxyNngSecret directive sets a pre-shared cluster secret. It must be configured with the same value on the reverse proxy and on every backend. The publisher signs each announcement with a keyed message-authentication code (a SipHash MAC) derived from the secret, together with a timestamp; the subscriber recomputes the MAC and checks the timestamp, dropping any announcement that is forged, tampered with, or replayed. Replayed messages are caught two ways: a freshness window (ProxyNngMaxSkew) rejects old timestamps, and a per-backend check rejects any announcement whose timestamp does not strictly advance, so a captured-and-resent message (for example, one replayed to keep a dead backend from being evicted) is dropped.

If ProxyNngSecret is set on the proxy, every announcement must carry a valid, recent MAC or it is rejected. If the secrets on the proxy and a backend differ, that backend's announcements are silently rejected (and logged), which appears as the backend never joining the balancer.

If no secret is configured the channel is unauthenticated and the proxy emits a warning when it starts listening. Because the secret is stored in the configuration file, restrict that file's permissions as you would for a private key.

note.title: Clock synchronisation
note.p: The timestamp-based replay protection compares the announcement's time against the proxy's clock, so the proxy and backends must have reasonably synchronised clocks (for example via NTP). See ProxyNngMaxSkew.

directivesynopsis.name: ProxyNngMaxSkew
directivesynopsis.description: Maximum allowed age of a signed announcement

usage.p: The ProxyNngMaxSkew directive sets the anti-replay window used when ProxyNngSecret is configured: the proxy rejects any announcement whose signed timestamp differs from the current time by more than this amount, in either direction. It uses the time-interval directive syntax and defaults to seconds.

If unset, the default is 30 seconds. A larger window tolerates greater clock skew between hosts; a smaller window bounds the freshness check. Note that the per-backend strictly-increasing-timestamp check (see ProxyNngSecret) blocks replays regardless of this window. This directive is used on the proxy.
